public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1065

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1065](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1065)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1065

/--
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k * q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$?

This is mentioned as B46
in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*
 -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1065.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * q + 1} := by
  sorry

/--
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k 3^l q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$, $l ≥ 0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1065.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k l, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * 3^l * q + 1} := by
  sorry

end Erdos1065

reformulations.difference: Guy's B46 asks whether infinitely many primes p satisfy (p−1)/P(p−1)=2^k, where P denotes the largest prime factor. Lean instead asks for a representation p=2^k*q+1 with an existentially quantified prime q.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For p>2, a representation p−1=2^k*q has largest prime factor q, since q is prime and q≥2. Conversely, the quotient condition gives the representation by taking q=P(p−1). Any convention at P(1) affects only p=2 and cannot affect infinitude. The full infinitude equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without sorry or dependence on the problem's admitted theorems.

could_not_verify: Erdos1065.erdos_1065.parts.ii: I could not conclusively verify the source's intended exponent bounds. The accessible Guy B46 excerpt states the form 2^k*3^l without specifying those bounds, while OEIS A339465 imposes positive exponents. That OEIS sequence may merely isolate the additional terms beyond part (i), so this is not evidence of a defect. Lean permits l=0, adding the entire part (i) family; this is not merely a finite boundary difference. I proved equivalence to the largest-prime-factor formulation with nonnegative exponents, but the inaccessible cited webpage prevented independently confirming that interpretation and reading its current remarks.
review.notes: No confirmed mathematical defect was found. Lean inspection confirms that p, q, k and l are all natural numbers and that both answer slots have the intended propositional scope. Boundary proofs and computations through p=100 behaved as expected. Both largest-prime-factor infinitude equivalences, with nonnegative exponents, were kernel-checked in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean. The community status database still records problem 1065 as open. Direct access to the cited Erdős Problems page and its forum was blocked despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so verification of part (ii) remains limited as described below.
